decontamination_notes: Real DOM-clobbering fail-open fix from cure53/DOMPurify PR #1560 ('fix: added better handling of clobbering via ownerDocument'), merged 2026-08-03 -- after the training cutoffs of the models evaluated here (e.g. Opus 5, May 2026), so the specific fix is not in their training data (decontaminated: true), with upstream_merged recorded as proof. HTMLFormElement carries [LegacyOverrideBuiltIns], so a form child named 'ownerDocument' (<input name="ownerDocument">, or a form-associated external input) shadows Node.prototype.ownerDocument: a direct form.ownerDocument read returns that element. DOMPurify's _createNodeIterator read the property directly and called createNodeIterator.call(<the clobbering element>, ...), which throws 'Illegal invocation'. On the IN_PLACE path that throw is raised BEFORE the sanitize walk's fail-closed exception barrier, so the caller's live tree is returned with every armed on-event handler un-neutralized -- a clobber that fully defeats sanitization. The fix reads ownerDocument through a cached Node.prototype getter (immune to the per-element shadow) at both _createNodeIterator and _scrubTemplateExpressions, and moves iterator construction inside the barrier so any residual failure still fails closed. The gold patch is the ownerDocument subset of the PR (the getOwnerDocument getter, the two clobber-safe reads, and the barrier move); the PR's orthogonal _forkSharedAllowlist hook-widening hardening, which the upstream tests do not exercise, is excluded. Slice at the PR base commit (21.9k LOC). Runs on a dedicated :node-dompurify image (node-ts + jsdom@29.1.1 baked in, pinned to DOMPurify's package-lock; resolved via NODE_PATH) so the slice ships without a committed node_modules and the network-off sandbox needs no installs. Hidden tests run tsx --test directly against src/purify.ts (no rollup build) with node:test, a jsdom window, and a VERSION shim for the build-time global. Coverage floor: 3 fail_to_pass (a clobbered ownerDocument leaving, respectively, a direct on-event handler, a deeply nested handler, and any serialized on-event handler un-stripped on the IN_PLACE path -- each armed at base because the iterator throws before the barrier) plus a 2-check regression guard (un-clobbered IN_PLACE sanitize still strips handlers; ordinary string sanitize keeps benign markup and drops dangerous attributes). MIT/Apache-2.0 (LICENSE, LICENSE-MPL) preserved.

fail_to_pass.name: clobber_nested_handler
fail_to_pass.cmd: tsx --test --test-name-pattern='^vb clobbered ownerDocument still neutralizes a deeply nested handler$' vb_ownerdoc.test.ts
